question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Fight tooth and nail
solution:
The correct answer is '**Fight very fiercely**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate meaning of the given idiom '**Fight tooth and nail**' is '**Fight very fiercely**'.
 
• Let’s look at the meaning and example of the given phrasal verb:
 
 
• **Fight tooth and nail**- "to try very hard to get something you want". (आप जो चाहते हैं उसे पाने के लिए बहुत मेहनत करना)
 
 
• E.g. *We **fought tooth and nail** to get the route of the new road changed.*
 
 
 
 
 
• *​​*Thus from the explanation given above, we find that the 3rd option is the correct choice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at the origin of the idiom:

 
 
• This idiom **dates back to the 1500s** and comes from the idea of fighting like a wild beast. Animals don’t have weapons, so they fight with everything that they’ve got: their teeth and nails.
